papers.title: Cell-Laden Biomimetically Mineralized Shark-Skin-Collagen-Based 3D Printed Hydrogels for the Engineering of Hard Tissues.
papers.abstract: Mineralization processes based on coprecipitation methods have been applied as a promising alternative to the most commonly used methods of polymer-ceramic combination, direct mixing, and incubation in simulated body fluid (SBF) or modified SBF. In the present study, for the first time, the in situ mineralization (ideally hydroxyapatite formation) of blue shark (Prionace glauca (PG)) collagen to fabricate 3D printable cell-laden hydrogels is proposed. In the first part, several parameters for collagen mineralization were tested until optimization. The hydroxyapatite formation was confirmed by FT-IR, XRD, and TEM techniques. In the second part, stable bioinks combining the biomimetically mineralized collagen with alginate (AG) (1:1, 1:2, 1:3, and AG) solution were used for 3D printing of hydrogels. The addition of Ca2+ ions into the system did present a synergistic effect: by one side, the in situ mineralization of the collagen occurred, and at same time, they were also useful to ionically cross-link the blends with alginate, avoiding the addition of any cytotoxic chemical cross-linking agent. Mouse fibroblast cell line survival during and after printing was favored by the presence of PG collagen as exhibited by the biological performance of the hydrogels. Inspired in a concept of marine byproduct valorization, 3D bioprinting of in situ mineralized blue shark collagen is thus proposed as a promising approach, envisioning the engineering of mineralized tissues.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何人工智能技术，与AI辅助生物打印方向不相关
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate any AI or machine learning methods for bioprinting workflow; it focuses purely on biomimetic collagen mineralization and cell-laden hydrogel printing.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发基于鲨鱼胶原的矿化生物墨水用于硬组织工程
summary_zh.method: 通过原位矿化法在鲨鱼胶原中形成羟基磷灰石，并与海藻酸钠混合制备可打印水凝胶
summary_zh.result: 矿化胶原生物墨水支持细胞存活且具有良好打印性
summary_zh.validation: 通过FT-IR、XRD、TEM表征矿化，并进行了细胞活性测试

summary_en.motivation: To develop a biomimetically mineralized collagen bioink from blue shark byproducts for 3D bioprinting of hard tissues.
summary_en.method: In situ mineralization of shark collagen was optimized to form hydroxyapatite, then blended with alginate to produce cell-laden printable hydrogels.
summary_en.result: The mineralized collagen bioink showed good printability and supported fibroblast viability during and after printing.
summary_en.validation: Mineralization was confirmed by FT-IR, XRD, and TEM; biological performance was evaluated via mouse fibroblast cell culture.
